D: A playboy millionaire must choose between his fortune and the working-class woman he loves.
P: Serve dessert when Hobson says something devastatingly dry.
S: Rye squares with smoked salmon, lemon crème fraîche and dill

Thin rye cut into squares, buttered, topped with smoked salmon, a dot of crème fraîche whipped with lemon, dill and cracked pepper. Butter 6 slices rye bread and cut into small squares. Top with 200g smoked salmon. Whip 100ml crème fraîche with lemon zest and put a dot on each, then add a dill sprig and cracked pepper. Serve cold.
Warm buckwheat blini, crème fraîche, salmon roe and snipped chives
Warm buckwheat blini at 180C for 5 minutes, top with crème fraîche, caviar or salmon roe and snipped chives.
Hobson the butler, keeping Arthur's world properly civilised

Crustless white bread with herbed cream cheese, paper-thin cucumber and peppery cress, cut into neat fingers. Peel and very thinly slice 1 telegraph cucumber, salt lightly for 10 minutes and pat dry. Beat 150g cream cheese with 2 tbsp chopped dill, lemon zest and pepper. Spread over 12 slices white bread. Top 6 with cucumber and a punnet of cress, close with the rest and press gently. Cut off the crusts and slice into 4 fingers each.
M: Topside roasted rare to medium rare, with gravy from the pan juices

Topside seasoned and roasted at 200C to 52C inside, rested, sliced thin, Yorkshire puddings and gravy. Roast a 1.5kg topside at 200C until 52C inside, about an hour, and rest 20 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs, 150g flour and 300ml milk, pour into very hot oiled tins and bake at 220C for 20 minutes. Make gravy with 400ml stock and pan juices.
Linda, the waitress who shoplifted a tie

Corned beef, Swiss and sauerkraut on rye with Russian dressing, fried in butter until crisp and melting. Mix 80g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp horseradish and 1 tbsp chopped gherkin for the dressing. Butter 8 slices rye on one side. On the unbuttered side spread dressing, then layer 400g sliced corned beef, 200g drained sauerkraut and 8 slices Swiss. Close and fry over medium heat for 4 minutes a side, pressing down, until crisp and melted.
W: Vanilla bean custard baked in ramekins under a crackly sugar crust
600ml cream infused with vanilla over 6 yolks and 80g sugar, baked in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes, chilled overnight, caster sugar torched to amber.
K: Champagne poured over a splash of crème de cassis

Crème de cassis in a chilled flute, topped with brut champagne and a fresh raspberry dropped in. Chill 4 flutes in the freezer for 10 minutes. Pour 15ml crème de cassis into each glass. Tilt each flute and top slowly with 120ml chilled brut champagne so it doesn't foam over, then let it settle. Drop a fresh raspberry into each glass so it bobs in the bubbles and serve straight away, before the fizz fades.

Top each square with a fold of beetroot, a small dot of creme fraiche, a dill sprig and cracked pepper.

dishes.make_ahead: Snip the chives up to 4 hours ahead; warm the blini and top them just before serving

steps.text: Warm the blini on a tray in a 180C oven.
Top each with a teaspoon of creme fraiche, a little roe and snipped chives.
Serve straight away on a silver tray if you have one.

veg.make_ahead: Lentils up to 2 days, keep chilled

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water until just tender, then drain.
Dress with the soy, lemon juice and oil and leave to cool.
Warm the blini on a tray in a 180C oven.
Top each with a teaspoon of creme fraiche, a little of the lentils and snipped chives.
Serve straight away on a silver tray if you have one.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the pudding batter up to 1 day ahead in the fridge; roast the beef and bake the puddings on the day

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Rub the beef with oil, salt and pepper.
Whisk the eggs, flour and milk into a smooth batter and leave to rest.
Roast the beef until the centre reads 52C on a probe.
Rest the beef under foil. Raise the oven to 220C, heat the oiled tins until smoking, pour in the batter and bake the puddings until risen and golden.
Make gravy by simmering the stock with the pan juices until slightly thickened. Carve and serve.

veg.make_ahead: Nut roast mix up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Fry the onion, garlic and mushrooms in the olive oil until dry.
Mix with the nuts, lentils, breadcrumbs, cheddar, thyme, 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, 2 of the eggs, salt and pepper, and press into a lined loaf tin.
Whisk the remaining 3 eggs, 140g of the flour and the milk into a smooth batter and leave to rest.
Bake the nut roast until firm and browned on top.
Rest the roast under foil. Raise the oven to 220C, heat the oiled tins until smoking, pour in the batter and bake the puddings until risen and golden.
Melt the butter, stir in the remaining flour, then whisk in the stock and remaining soy sauce and simmer until slightly thickened. Slice the roast and serve.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 2 days, keep chilled before torching

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150C. Warm the cream with the split vanilla bean until steaming.
Whisk the yolks and sugar, then pour the cream over, whisking gently. Strain into ramekins.
Stand the ramekins in a tray of hot water and bake until just set with a wobble.
Cool, then chill overnight. Chilling counts toward the cooking time.
Sprinkle with sugar and torch to amber.

dishes.make_ahead: Chill the champagne in the fridge up to 1 day ahead; freeze the flutes 10 minutes before pouring

steps.text: Chill the flutes in the freezer.
Pour the cassis into each glass, tilt and top slowly with champagne so it does not foam over.
Drop a raspberry into each glass and serve straight away.

steps.text: Chill the flutes in the freezer.

Drop a raspberry into each glass and serve straight away.
